reviewHistory.summary: T874 free-kick timing and its observer are coherent with the stated offside rules, and the bounded T873 port preserves recorded facts in the supplied evidence. One T873 pressure-release contract gap remains: through passes bypass the new release watch and still hold for their full scripted duration under continuous close pressure.

findings.message: The new MATCH-12 close-pressure release rule is not applied to through passes. performPass immediately delegates beat.through to performThrough, whose kickReady() unconditionally waits until left() <= 0 and never consults pressedOff/holdOver. A focused valid stage with ordinary escape=0, actor 5 at [45,30], receiver 8 initially onside at [68,30], hold=8, target [90,30], and defender 17 tracking 1.5 m from the carrier kicks only at t=8.0 s; the opponent stays within 1.590 m for all 8 s. Raw reproduction: /tmp/nf14-engine-through-repro.json on ba8feee4. Apply the shared pressure-release policy to legal through-pass timing while preserving receiver legality, bounded travel and recorded offside outcomes. Add a fast handler-level regression for the normal 0.4 s reaction and press-resistant 2.5 s case, with the existing through/offside tests retained.

review.summary: Fresh review of ffc79d52 confirms the strict-comparison gap is fixed: canonical actual settled records (excluding only documented script-derived material) and every frozen squad value are compared in addition to provenance metadata. Object key normalization preserves array/value semantics. Independent reproduction using the real baseline now rejects stale-hash score and squad-attribute mutations, while accepting material/key-order and engine-SHA differences with equal facts; evidence /tmp/nf14-viewer-record-fresh-repro.json. The four new regressions also cover changed player counters and permitted frame differences. Renderer, clock, resources and exporter are unchanged from the prior full review; no remaining P1/P2 found. Final paired HTML/browser/full verification remain coordinator gates.

reviewHistory.summary: The offline two-pitch implementation uses shared presentation helpers, resource-backed copy and verbatim identity parameters, with consistent browser-smoke evidence. The strict input/fact comparison guard is incomplete: it compares claimed metadata digests without validating the actual record and squads carried by each export.

findings.message: readExport() checks only the format of the claimed SHA fields, and assertComparable() compares those metadata strings but never validates or compares the actual playback.record or squads. The explicit MATCH-40/acceptance rule requires differing settled records or fixture inputs to fail the comparison build. Reproduction from the real delivery baseline: structuredClone the parsed export, change playback.record.score.home from 1 to 2 while leaving its metadata in place, then assertComparable(original, readExport(changed)); it succeeds and the page can claim the same facts while carrying different actual results. Evidence: /tmp/nf14-viewer-record-repro.json on 55a4f847. Validate the actual content against its digests and/or compare canonical actual records (excluding only documented script-derived material) and frozen squads/input fields before accepting the pair. Add focused stale-hash/changed-record and changed-squad regressions; retain acceptance of different staged frames and engine SHAs with equal facts.

review.summary: Independent review of f5b202ed (runtime881917b3) finds the bounded geometry and its single world integration consistent with T876/MATCH-17. The helper evaluates all opponent positions, preserves x and existing nearby-marker avoidance, chooses only strict improvements within unmark.step/pitch margins, and retains original targets for excluded participants/phases/orders/cues or no improvement. Direct on-shoulder/keeper movement and individual lag remain in the existing world flow. Independent geometry reproduction confirms the central screen improves, an open lane stays exact, an additional blocker selects the other side, and blocked alternatives retain the original; /tmp/nf14-support-repro.json. Runtime code draws no RNG and mutates no record/script. Measurement evidence names the correct predecessor7e80480c and candidate881917b3 with exact per-seed record/script equality; it honestly reports the small aggregate support proxy gain, viewer-4 worsening and pressure/circle/stick tradeoffs without threshold changes. No P1/P2 found. Final integrated browser/full checks remain coordinator gates.

review.summary: T884 prior P2 is repaired on ad982d1e: cancellation snapshots the owned PID/parent/start identities, signals descendants before the immediate child, discovers children of surviving owned processes, and escalates matching survivors after the bounded grace without detaching from the outer Gusta process group. Independently reran all ten focused unit cases successfully (2.13 s, /tmp/nf14-t884-rereview-unit.log). Independent tiny probes verified the original inherited-pipe descendant is gone and terminal cancelled receipt resolves in 575 ms, a signal-resistant direct child records actual SIGKILL after 553 ms, and a late cleanup child is discovered/escalated and gone after 568 ms; an unrelated sibling sentinel remains alive in all three. Full stdout/stderr paths and cancellation/command/signal provenance remain readable and distinct. Raw probe command/source/results are /tmp/nf14-t884-rereview-probes.mts and .jsonl. Existing verification command/phase/tier/test-timeout definitions are preserved. No remaining P1/P2 in the scoped change; actual batch execution remains coordinator-owned.

reviewHistory.summary: T884 retains full logs and truthful process/reporter failures, but catchable cancellation can leave nested command processes alive and never emit the promised terminal receipt.

findings.message: cancel() signals only the immediate child. A command that spawns a long-lived child with inherited stdout/stderr exits on SIGTERM while its descendant survives and holds the pipes open; Node never emits the immediate child close event, so run.done and verify.mjs remain waiting with only a cancelling receipt. Reproduced on the fixed submission with two tiny Node processes: after 500 ms done=false, lastStatus=cancelling and grandchildAlive=true; the terminal receipt appeared only after explicit grandchild cleanup. The real stages run through pnpm and can have the same process nesting. Make cancellation terminate the owned command subtree and finish its terminal/log receipt within a bounded cleanup period, while retaining outer-Gusta cancellation containment; add a focused nested-child cancellation regression rather than a full-suite test. Raw reproduction: /tmp/nf14-t884-review-descendant.mts and /tmp/nf14-t884-review-descendant.jsonl. All nine submitted tiny-child tests independently pass (/tmp/nf14-t884-review-unit.log), but none exercises descendants.
